_: How a field battle plays (army_skirmish.gd, army_melee.gd and combat.gd read it through data.gd; docs/TUNING.md). hp: blows a soldier takes. hit.beaten, hit.victors: a blow's chance to land, by side. kickLands: a kick's chance to land. dodge: the chance a blow that misses is a dodge rather than a parry. kickOdds: how often a swordsman kicks instead of cutting. breakAt: the beaten side runs when this share of it is left. longest: seconds at blows before whatever is left runs. charge.passes: a knight's charges through the line. charge.ride: a knight's charge speed, units a second. floored: the chance a heavy blow that doesn't kill knocks a man down. field: the massed battle of two hosts (army_field.gd on army.gd's regiments): gap, the lines' middles apart when they deploy; start, seconds both lines stand before it begins; advance, the foot's pace to contact (units a second); contact, the gap between front ranks at blows; longest, seconds at blows before the beaten break whatever their strength. volley: seconds between an archer regiment's volleys (low, high), arrows in one, their flight (seconds) and arc (height over distance), men it fells (low, high), and how near the lines may come before archers stop (until). fight: men a regiment in contact loses a second (beaten, victors; the outcome is the realm's, Freeciv's), seconds between a front man's blows (low, high), the chance a front man reels instead (hitOdds) or takes a blow on his shield (blockOdds), ranks that fight, how far the front surges, and how much harder a flanked regiment bleeds. cavalry: ride and charge pace, how far round the enemy's end it swings (wide) and how far behind its front it turns in (behind). waver: strength below which a beaten regiment's banner wavers; rout: below which it breaks; run: its pace in flight; scatter: how far each running man drifts a second; fade: seconds before the routed are gone. camera: the lens's quarter off the lines and how fast it follows. field.play: battles in play (scenes.gd stages one where the bridge tells of a battle): on (or --battles=field), the lines' middles apart there, men in a regiment for each company that fought, the most companies shown a side, how many such battles at once (more are the small skirmish), seconds the field stays held before it's gone. field.turns: bearings tried round the crown's muster for the foe's line, the one on the most fit ground taken; field.frontage: men abreast in a battle regiment (low, high), deeper blocks than the muster's line. skirmish.*: the small battle of two lines (scene_kinds/battle.gd fight): ranks and files a side, gap between files, row between ranks, reach (half the gap between two duelists), knights on the wing, field (how far the fight reaches from its centre). ground.*: where a battle may be fought (battlefield): rise (the most the ground may rise or fall across the field), rings (how far out, in rings 0.8 apart, it is looked for), town_clear (how far its edge keeps from a town), farm_clear (its centre from a farmstead, past the field), rough (what each kind of land costs it).
